name: Gresi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only subclassification refs (Anceaux 1965 wordlists; Fautngil 2009) on Glottolog; no grammar/phonology located

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open repository, hdl 1885/146624; text kept)
sources.note: Language index 'Gresi (NE IJ, W of L Sentani; also Gresik)' lists only survey/index items: Barr & Barr 1978 Index of Irian Jaya languages, Kana 1975 Languages of Kabupaten Jayapura (MS), Silzer & Heikkinen Clouse index, Voegelin & Voegelin 1965, Voorhoeve 1975, Wurm & Hattori 1981. No descriptive work on Gresi up to 1996 (Kemtuk has van der Wilden & van der Wilden 1975 phonology, van der Wilden 1976, 1981 grammar MS).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and langdoc listing for gres1240 (Hammarström et al. 2025)
sources.note: 5 refs total: Purba et al. 2002, Udam 2014, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994 (wordlists), Voorhoeve 1975 (wordlists), anon. 1973 (customary-law ethnography, 'Genyem, Kemtuk/Gressi'). No phonology-type reference exists for Gresi.

sources.citation: Fautngil, Chris. 2009. Language varieties in Grime Valley Jayapura: Regional dialectological study. E-Journal Universitas Udayana 3(1): 1-6.
sources.note: Only recent comparative note covering Kemtuk-Gresi varieties; could contain phonological comparisons. Udayana OJS refused connections from here.

sources.citation: Fields, Philip C. 1991. A phonology of the Orya language. In Tom Dutton (ed.), Papers in Papuan Linguistics No. 1. Pacific Linguistics A-73. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open repository, hdl 1885/145736)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Single mention (note 2): Orya 'bears little similarity in cognates or structure to Kemtuk-Gresi or Nimboran'. No Gresi phonology.

sources.citation: van der Wilden, Jaap & Jelly van der Wilden. 1975. Kemtuk phonology. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development 4(3): 31-60. (papuaweb mirror via the Internet Archive 2004-12-14, image-only scan; Kemtuk pages scanned)
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE Kemtuk (kemt1242), not Gresi. Gresi appears only as a separate language in the 1975 SIL cognate table (Kemtuk-Gresi 80%, p. 32). For Kemtuk (pp. 32-33): phonological words 'are of two general contrastive classes: ultimate stress and penultimate stress' (lexical contrast). No Gresi data; not transferable.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open repository, hdl 1885/146481)
sources.note: Entry 95 GRESI (Gresik), group IXb: dialects '?', villages '?', sources Cowan 1952c, 1957b; Anceaux 1965. A bare wordlist column (unmarked for stress). No stress statement; the introduction says the wordlist orthography is not phonemic.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. The Nimboran sub-phylum-level family (sec. 2.6.2.2.15). In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, pp. 421-422. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open repository, hdl 1885/145150)
sources.note: p. 421: lists Gresik among the five members and states 'For the other languages in the family the only data at hand are wordlists of Anceaux' collection.' p. 422, for Nimboran only: 'The language is non-tonal; stress is phonemic.' Nothing on Gresi stress.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1965. The Nimboran Language: Phonology and Morphology. Verhandelingen KITLV 44. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. xi+246 pp. (OAPEN open-access scan, archive.org item oapen-20.500.12657-32235)
sources.note: Describes NIMBORAN only. Gresi is named on pp. 1-2 (Gresi and Kamtuk 'most closely related'; five-language subgroup) and once in a phonology footnote (word-final glottal stop avoided as 'an undignified imitation of the Gresi language'). Ch. VII 'The accent' (pp. 36-39) is about Nimboran: accent = higher pitch usually with stress, one per word, 'there is no rule by which the place of the accent in all words is determined' (p. 37). No statement about Gresi stress anywhere (all 5 'Gresi' hits in the text checked).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Gresi language' and 'Nimboran languages'; Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Gresi'
sources.note: No phonology or stress information; references are Ethnologue, Glottolog, Foley 2018, Voorhoeve 1975, Ross 2005.
